title: Paediatric nephrology essentials

steps.tx: Primary idiopathic nephrotic syndrome in childhood is **steroid-sensitive** (**SSNS**) in over **85%** to **90%** of presentations, exhibiting dramatic proteinuria remission with oral glucocorticoids. Histopathologically, **minimal change disease** accounts for greater than **80%** of cases presenting between ages **1** and **6** years, presenting with heavy selective proteinuria and absence of macroscopic hematuria.

steps.tx: In children presenting with primary **steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome** (**SRNS**), monogenic mutations in essential podocyte architectural genes account for up to **30%** of cases. Genetic evaluation frequently uncovers mutations in **NPHS1** (encoding nephrin), **NPHS2** (encoding podocin), the Wilms tumor suppressor gene **WT1**, or the basement membrane laminin gene **LAMB2**.

Genetic evaluation frequently uncovers mutations in NPHS1 encoding nephrin, NPHS2 encoding podocin, the Wilms tumor suppressor gene WT1, or the basement membrane laminin gene LAMB2.

left.title: Genetic SRNS Podocytopathies
points: Low risk of post-transplant FSGS recurrence

right.title: Immunological Idiopathic SRNS
points: Managed with plasma exchange and rituximab

steps.tx: Infantile **Congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type** (**CNF**) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic mutations in **NPHS1**, disrupting the slit diaphragm scaffold protein **nephrin**. Presenting with massive in utero proteinuria, an extraordinarily **huge placenta** exceeding **25%** of birth weight, and severe anasarca within the first **3** months of life.
steps.say: Infantile Congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic mutations in NPHS1, disrupting the slit diaphragm scaffold protein nephrin. It presents with massive in utero proteinuria, an extraordinarily huge placenta exceeding 25% of birth weight, and severe anasarca within the first 3 months of life.

nodes.label: Placenta > 25% of birth weight, severe prenatal proteinuria
Refractory nephrotic syndrome requiring bilateral nephrectomy

steps.tx: Dominant point mutations in the zinc-finger region of the **WT1 gene** involving exon **8** or **9** cause **Denys-Drash syndrome**. Clinical presentation is defined by the diagnostic triad of early-onset **diffuse mesangial sclerosis** (**DMS**), male pseudohermaphroditism with **XY disorder of sex development**, and an extremely high risk of embryonic **Wilms tumor**.

Clinical presentation is defined by the diagnostic triad of early-onset diffuse mesangial sclerosis, male pseudohermaphroditism with XY disorder of sex development, and an extremely high risk of embryonic Wilms tumor.

vis.alt: WAGR syndrome and WT1 gene-associated renal dysgenesis
vis.caption: WT1 zinc-finger mutations, diffuse mesangial sclerosis, and Wilms tumor risk (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Alternative splice donor site mutations in intron **9** of the **WT1** gene produce **Frasier syndrome**, which characteristically presents with late-onset steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with **FSGS** histology. Affected individuals demonstrate complete male sex reversal (**46,XY females**) with streak gonads and high predisposition to developing malignant **gonadoblastoma**.

left.title: Frasier Syndrome
points: FSGS histology with late-onset nephrotic syndrome

right.title: Denys-Drash Syndrome
points: WT1 exon 8 or 9 missense point mutation
Extreme early risk of Wilms tumor

steps.tx: In male infants, **Posterior urethral valves** (**PUV**) represent the most frequent cause of severe congenital lower urinary tract obstruction. Classical antenatal sonographic features demonstrate bilateral **hydroureteronephrosis**, marked oligohydramnios, and a massively distended, thick-walled bladder with a dilated posterior urethra producing the pathognomonic **keyhole sign**.

nodes.label: Bladder dilation with pathognomonic keyhole sign

steps.tx: Pediatric hypertension is defined statistically by systolic or diastolic blood pressure >= **95th percentile** for child age, sex, and height on **3** or more separate visits. Unlike essential hypertension in adults, secondary hypertension accounts for over 85% of childhood cases, with underlying **reflux nephropathy** and glomerulonephritis representing the predominant etiologies.
steps.say: Pediatric hypertension is defined statistically by systolic or diastolic blood pressure at or above the 95th percentile for child age, sex, and height on 3 or more separate visits. Unlike essential hypertension in adults, secondary hypertension accounts for over 85% of childhood cases, with underlying reflux nephropathy and glomerulonephritis representing the predominant etiologies.

steps.tx: Primary monosymptomatic **nocturnal enuresis** in children aged **5** years or older arises from nocturnal polyuria, bladder detrusor overactivity, and impaired arousal from sleep. Initial non-pharmacological management utilizes **enuresis alarm** conditioning, with oral **desmopressin** (melt formulation) serving as effective first-line medical therapy.
